To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CC stretching phonon modes of the trans-1,3-butadiene chain are not only different in frequency from the ones of the cis-isomer but also different for each chain-length, and that the electron phonon coupling is strong enough to be detected by means of the vibrational spectra.
the experimental phonon dispersion curve of polyenes is not a constant but depends on the chain length.

the experimental phonon dispersion relations of polyenals are not the same for each chain length, that the CC stretching modes are not degenerate in polyenals, that the CC modes are coupled to other modes in polyenals and that the coupling is different in different polyene chains, and that the CC modes of polyenals couple to the C=O stretching mode.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental and theoretical study of the infrared and Rama spectra of polyenals and polyenes and their relation to phonon dispersion curves.
the study of the phonon dispersion curves in a series of polyenes and the electron phonon coupling (EPC) in these systems.
the experimental and theoretical investigation of the vibrational properties of a series of linear conjugated polyene derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CC stretching phonon frequencies are strongly dependent on the chain length and that the electron phonon coupling is not negligible in the polyenals.
the CC stretching modes are very sensitive to the length of the chain and to the presence of the C=O group.
the experimental phonon dispersion curve for each chain length is a superposition of the phonon curves of the shorter chains and the phonon dispersion curves for the longer chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to show the existence of a series of CC stretching phonon modes with different dispersion relations for each chain length which are strongly coupled with the electronic states.
we have been able to derive, for the first, time experimental phonon dispersion curve for the CC stretching modes in a series of polyene derivatives.
we were able to derive the CC stretching phonon dispersions for a series of polyene derivatives with the aid of a combination of experimental and quantum chemical data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron phonon coupling (EPC), which is a measure of the interaction of the vibrational degrees of freedom with the electronic ones, is strongly chain length dependent.
we are able to derive experimental CC stretching phonon frequencies and dispersion curves which are not available in the literature.
the electron phonon coupling (EPC) is a strong function of the chain length and the EPC strength increases with the chain length.
